question: Does a newly published Looc Lake paper add a Central Luzon freshwater source lead, and is the available abstract detailed enough for species-level admission?

sourceDocument.title: Water Quality Parameters, Freshwater Fish Assemblages and Anthropogenic Disturbances in Looc Lake, Castillejos, Zambales, Philippines

studyScopeAsReportedInAbstract.waterbodyType: shallow tropical floodplain lake; freshwater fish assemblage study
studyScopeAsReportedInAbstract.stationDescription: Eastern, western, northern, southern and central lake areas
studyScopeAsReportedInAbstract.deploymentDuration: four hours per station, as reported in the abstract

abstractFindingsAsReported.authorClassification: The abstract classifies all eight recorded species as non-native and describes Sarotherodon melanotheron as the dominant invasive species.
abstractFindingsAsReported.interpretation: These are aggregate claims in the indexed abstract. Seven species names, the underlying table, specimen evidence and the authors' classification basis have not been reviewed. This is not an occurrence dataset or current lake checklist.

accessAndReuse.publisherPageResult: A direct page request on 2026-11-24 returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare browser challenge. Publisher-indexed search text exposed article metadata and the abstract.
accessAndReuse.fullText: Not retrieved or reviewed; no PDF or supplement retained.
accessAndReuse.reuseDisposition: No item-specific permission was verified. Do not reproduce tables, figures, images or article prose.

evidenceDecision.decision: Record Looc Lake as a new freshwater source lead. Keep the abstract's eight-species and non-native statements as source-reported aggregate claims only; do not admit the single named abstract taxon or infer current presence from this screen.

limitations: The abstract provides no collection dates, specimen vouchers, coordinates, or station-level species list.
Seven of the eight species are unnamed in the indexed abstract text reviewed here.
Taxonomic identity, native-range status and the paper's invasive classification have not been independently cross-checked.
The publisher page's HTTP 403 response is an access limitation for this review and does not establish that the article is unavailable through other lawful routes.
The abstract does not establish current fish presence, safety, fishing access, legality, catchability, diet or bait recommendations.
nextStep: Seek a lawful full-text or author/institution repository copy, then review the species table, field dates, station allocation, vouchers, taxonomy, duplicate-study lineage and article-specific reuse terms before considering any public adaptation. Central Luzon and Luzon remain incomplete.
